plain_english: The entry is the testament dative and inventory of John Glasgow, resident at Quodquen (Quothquan) in Libberton parish, Lanarkshire. It says that he died during an unread month in 1661 and inventories his moveable estate before calculating the distributable portion.

The second part records commissary James Hamilton's confirmation and the authority of an executor dative to administer the goods and debts. The executor's name and the words immediately describing that person are not secure enough in these scans to establish a family relationship.
The John entry ends near the top of image 139. The clearly separate James testament beginning below it is outside this transcription.
findings: The manuscript identifies the deceased as John Glasgow in Quodquen, within Libberton parish and the sheriffdom of Lanark.
The death is placed in 1661, before the indexed/registration date of 13 January 1662; the month is not securely legible.
The record contains an inventory, debt calculation and commissary confirmation, but most individual goods and monetary amounts remain unread.

The earlier proposed reading 'John Glasgow lawfull sone' at the head of image 139 is not secure in context. Neither 'lawfull' nor a following kinship word is clear enough to promote from the faded, tightly written passage; no parent-child conclusion is made.
James Hamilton acts as commissary in the confirmation clause. That official role does not identify him as executor or kin.
The James testament beginning lower on image 139 is a new record and has been excluded.
changes_from_previous: Replaced a three-line selective extract with sequential working lines covering the whole John entry across both supplied images.
Read the locality as Quodquen in Libberton parish and recorded the manuscript's 1661 death-year statement separately from the 1662 registration date.
Rejected the former 'lawfull sone' assertion because the words following John Glasgow, their grammatical subject and the executor's identity are not securely established.
Distinguished full supplied-entry coverage from partial decipherment and explicitly bounded the adjacent preceding and following entries.
